sop-from-memo.output:
Water Heater Swap — Maple & Sons Plumbing

YOU WILL NEED
- Main water shut-off valve (at meter or entry)
- Breaker panel access
- Garden hose (from van)
- Floor drain or bucket
- New water heater (sized for home)
- New flex supply lines (both hot and cold)
- Wrench set
- Camera or phone (for photo)

STEPS

1. Shut off water at the main valve — turn clockwise until it stops. Do not rely on the isolation valve under the tank.

2. Kill the breaker for the water heater at the electrical panel — flip the switch to OFF.

3. Attach the garden hose to the drain valve at the base of the old tank. Run the hose to the floor drain or a bucket. Open the drain valve and let the tank empty completely.

4. Disconnect the old supply lines from the top of the tank using a wrench. Disconnect the vent pipe if present.

5. Drain any remaining water from the lines into a bucket.

6. Haul the old tank out. Set the new tank in place, level.

7. Connect new flex supply lines (hot and cold) to the new tank inlet and outlet. Do not reuse old lines even if they look fine.

8. Open the main water valve slowly to fill the new tank.

9. Open the closest faucet (hot side) to bleed air from the lines. Leave it open until water runs steady with no sputtering. Close the faucet.

10. Switch the breaker back ON at the panel.

11. Wait 20 minutes. Check the tank, all connections and the floor around it for drips or leaks.

12. Take a photo of the completed installation and new tank serial number for the file.

DONE LOOKS LIKE
- Old tank removed, new tank in place and level
- All connections tight, no water dripping after 20 minutes
- Heater powered on, pilot or heating element active (if applicable)
- Photo in customer file with date and technician name

COMMON MISTAKES & HOW TO CHECK

1. Forgetting the expansion tank or not checking for a check valve on the main. If the main has a check valve, the expansion tank must be in place or pressure will build and crack the new tank. Check: Ask the owner if they know of a check valve at the meter. If unsure, ASK OWNER before filling.

2. Rushing the air bleed step. Turning the breaker on before the lines are full of water can damage the heating element. Check: Make sure water flows steady from the faucet and no air bubbles come out before you flip the breaker.

3. Not waiting 20 minutes to inspect for leaks. A slow drip at a fitting may not show up in the first 2 minutes. Check: Set a timer. Walk back in 20 minutes and inspect every connection, the floor and under the tank with a flashlight.
—
NOTES FOR OWNER
- Expansion tank check valve step is marked ASK OWNER — you know your service area. Add the detail about how you check or who calls if a check valve is found.
- All times and tool names are from your transcript; no numbers invented.
- Ready to send to a new hire or print for the truck. Edit as needed, then delete this section.
